messages:
maria: Quick follow-up to the allocator spike: I prototyped a NUMA-aware "shadow" mapping that keeps a tiny CPU-side page directory for each large allocation. It records residency, last-touch, and a migration epoch so we can move blocks without reshaping high-level tensor objects.
kevin: Can you outline the invariants you expect? shadow entry points to host-page or gpu-page handle? :thinking:
maria: Exactly. Each shadow entry stores: residency enum (GPU/Host/Remote), physical handle, epoch, and in-use ref bit. The runtime consults it on misses.
anya: Sounds like another indirection. How bad is the hot-path cost?
maria: We only touch it on first access or on explicit migration checks. Hot-path (fast KV path) keeps pinned GPU pointers for cached ranges. The shadow read is on fallback paths.
sam: Fragmentation concern: if we slice tensors into many 4K entries, we could bloat the allocator metadata and create many tiny GPU fragments.
kevin: Agreed. Plan: per-model "arena" slabs sized to match observed tensor footprints (e.g., 2M slabs for kv, 8M for activations). Shadow entries support base page (4K) + superpage (2M) coalescing bits.
anya: We'll need a background coalescer and an opportunistic compactor. Do we want synchronous compaction during allocation failure?
maria: No blocking compaction. Strategy: async coalescer that runs when free small-page ratio > threshold or during low-util windows. On allocation miss we try quick local compaction (merge adjacent free descriptors) with a short budget, then fall back to on-device fallback if still insufficient.
runtime-bot: deploy: allocator/shadow-mapping spike deployed to staging-canary at 2025-12-02T09:40Z
kevin: Migration semantics: do migrations happen synchronously on fault or via async prefetch with a short stall?
maria: Async prefetch + singleflight per page key. First waiter triggers DMA, others await promise. If DMA doesn't complete within deadline (configurable, default 25ms) we try a local on-device fallback path (quantized variant or smaller KV chunk) and record a migration stall metric.
sam: How to avoid thundering-herd on startup when many layers fault?
anya: Add jitter + leader election per page key (singleflight). Also prefetch heuristics: warm first N layers based on model profile during cold-start.
kevin: Ops/telemetry: expose page_fault_rate, migration_latency_p50/p90/p99, small_page_fragment_ratio, superpage_utilization, cross_node_evictions. Add span labels for model_id, request_id.
maria: GC: heavyweight consolidator runs during low-util windows, migrates cold GPU pages back to host and coalesces free ranges into superpages. Controlled by autoscaler hints so we don't fight the scheduler.
sam: Edge: what if GC starts while a kernel references pages? Need robust in-use detection.
maria: Per-page refcounts + in-use bit set by enqueue time and cleared on completion callbacks. GC checks in-use and epoch; will skip in-flight pages. If a page is pinned by a long-running CUDA stream we skip and mark for next window.
anya: Driver interfaces: Linux path uses cudaHostRegister / mmap + vfio for some setups. We'll add an abstraction layer so backend-specific pin/unpin lives behind a thin shim. Track pinned page ceiling to avoid hitting driver limits.
kevin: Implementation roadmap (short):
```
1) lightweight shadow page table proto inside arena allocators
2) singleflight migration service + jittered prefetch
3) background coalescer + GC window hooks
4) metrics + alerts + canary runs
```

maria: Timeline: 1 week spike (microbench) -> 4 week prototype (migration + singleflight) -> 6 week feature polish (coalescer, GC, metrics).
sam: Risks: syscall/pin overheads and driver limits (pinned pages per process), migration tail latencies, and memory-accounting bugs. We'll measure syscall counts and add batching where it hurts.
anya: Action items:
- kevin: experiment with per-layer slab sizes and produce a size histogram (+10d)
- anya: design compaction policy and coalescer tuning (+14d)
- sam: add telemetry hooks and singleflight primitives (+7d)
- maria: run migration microbench across instance types and post numbers (+7d)
kevin: @maria please paste perf numbers and the staging canary link when available.
maria: microbench: async DMA 2M superpage median ~1.6ms on p4-like instance, p99 ~9-13ms depending on bus contention. These are preliminary. Will iterate.
anya: If p99 stays < 20ms it's acceptable for conservative SLAs; we'll gate on telemetry.
sam: I'll create an alert for migration_p99 > 30ms on staging.
maria: OK keeping thread open for follow-ups. Drop comments if you want different defaults for deadlines or if you see a hole in refcount handling. :slightly_smiling_face:
